title: TRUSS: Towards Task-Reliable and User-Safe Automated Agent Skill Generation

visual_explainer.blocker: Two isolated paper-specific GPT Image attempts in this run (CABLE and ArborMem) both ignored their grounded single-paper briefs and rendered a generic Agent Memory Radar dashboard with fabricated paper metadata. Visual QA rejected both; further required-paper retries were stopped to avoid publishing ungrounded visuals until the paper-identity failure is resolved.

analysis.tldr: TRUSS treats generated skills as executable persistent artifacts that must pass both static obligations and shadow execution before promotion: a brokered sandbox records provenance-preserving traces, a function/safety record drives refinement, and already-satisfied obligations must remain preserved across versions.
analysis.problem: LLM-generated skills can look plausible while making false function claims, unsafe tool calls, or hidden side effects. Text-only review misses runtime behavior, while execution-only checks may not encode explicit safety obligations or preserve evidence across iterative repairs.
analysis.core_idea: Generate a skill package, run a static checker over functional claims and nine safety properties, then execute the skill in a controlled shadow agent with brokered tools and an intermediate breaker. Convert the trace into Function/Safety Records, refine only evidence-bearing content, version the candidate by digest, and rerun the full check while preserving obligations that already passed.

memory_design.write: Generate and iteratively refine versioned skill packages containing natural-language procedure and executable resources.
memory_design.organize: Track explicit function/safety obligations plus provenance-preserving runtime traces and per-version Function/Safety Records.
memory_design.read: A shadow agent executes the skill through brokered tools; static and dynamic evidence determines whether the artifact is safe/reliable enough to promote.
memory_design.update_forget: The refiner edits failed evidence-bearing content and reruns all obligations while preserving previously satisfied ones; general skill aging/deletion is outside scope.

compared_to: Static checking alone versus the full static + shadow-execution + refinement stack
No-skill and intermediate-generation baselines on SkillGenBench
Matched clean/injected skill pairs on SkillInject
analysis.evidence: On 84 matched SkillInject clean/injected pairs (168 artifacts), the LLM checker has 44.64% precision/19.05% recall, static checking reaches 81.55/94.05, and the full TRUSS check reaches 100/100. On SkillSafetyBench, attack success falls 38.71→19.35 for GPT-5.5 and 46.45→29.68 for GPT-5.4 with zero reported attack regression, but safe-task completion differs sharply by target model (52.90 vs 23.87). On SkillGenBench, effectiveness rises 17.11 no-skill→29.95 intermediate LLM→52.94 TRUSS while security rises 50.80→75.40→100; the intermediate→TRUSS delta combines checking, execution, and refinement.
analysis.why_it_matters: TRUSS makes procedural-memory promotion a certification problem: a reusable skill is not trustworthy because its text is coherent, but because its claimed function and safety properties survive controlled execution and evidence-preserving refinement.
limitations: The safety property set and benchmarks are controlled and may miss open-world side effects, cross-tool interactions, or organization-specific policy constraints.
The strongest generation gain attributes to the full inspection/execution/refinement package rather than one isolated component.
Safe-task completion is highly target-model-dependent, limiting claims that a certified skill transfers uniformly across executors.
The work focuses on acquisition/promotion of generated skills, not long-term library retrieval, deprecation, or descendant revocation.
